e: Squamous-to-columnar (intestinal) metaplasia c̅ goblet cells defines Barrett's esophagus.
Incomplete penetrance → an obligate carrier remains unaffected, giving the appearance of a skipped generation.
Polyarteritis nodosa is the classic example of a medium-vessel vasculitis.
Masson trichrome selectively stains collagen/fibrosis (blue-green) against red-staining muscle.
β-thalassemia major: imbalanced globin chain synthesis → precipitated α-chains cause marrow precursor apoptosis → ineffective erythropoiesis.
Microcytic anemia (MCV 68) c̅ low ferritin = iron deficiency anemia.
IHC uses labelled antibodies to detect specific antigens/proteins directly in FFPE tissue sections.
RA c̅ nephrotic-range proteinuria + apple-green birefringence = secondary (AA) amyloidosis from chronic inflammation.
Post-streptococcal GN: EM shows subepithelial electron-dense 'humps' (immune complex deposits).
1-3 days post-MI: coagulative necrosis c̅ dense neutrophilic infiltration is the dominant histological finding.
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is linked to EBV, not CMV.
PSC: concentric 'onion-skin' periductal fibrosis c̅ beaded bile ducts.

Only 4 is correct: Giemsa stains mast cell granules purple.
Perls – iron (blue); alizarin red – Ca (red); Van Gieson – collagen (red).
Mitochondrial disease hits high-energy tissues – cardiac & skeletal muscle (cardiomyopathy, myopathy).

Major: carditis, chorea, polyarthritis (polyarthralgia in high-risk groups), nodules, erythema marginatum.
PR prolongation is minor.

Peutz-Jeghers: autosomal dominant, STK11 (LKB1) mutation, arborising hamartomatous polyps.
CHRPE belongs to FAP.
Lipids dissolve during routine processing – need frozen section (Oil red O/Sudan).

MCL: t(11;14) → cyclin D1 + SOX11 positive.
CD200 & CD23 negative (positive in CLL).

Microcytosis (MCV <80): iron deficiency, thalassemia, lead poisoning.
B12 deficiency → macrocytic.
Mentzer index <13 (RBC count ↑) → thalassemia trait; confirm c̅ Hb electrophoresis/HPLC.

Gaucher: glucocerebrosidase deficiency (crumpled-tissue-paper macrophages).
Ceramidase deficiency = Farber disease.
Rheumatic fever is pancarditis (pericarditis, myocarditis, endocarditis).
Prader-Willi: paternal 15q11-q13 deletion → hypotonia, hyperphagia/obesity, hypogonadism.
Nephrotic syndrome: proteinuria >3.5 g/day + hypoalbuminemia (oedema, hyperlipidemia are consequences).

RB: loss-of-function (two-hit) mutation; ↑ risk of osteosarcoma.
Active RB is hypophosphorylated; 'guardian of the genome' = p53.
Microcytic hypochromic anaemia c̅ target cells & normal/↑ RBC count → Hb electrophoresis confirms hemoglobinopathy.
Armanni-Ebstein (glycogen in tubular cells) is a rare change; podocyte loss, mesangial widening and GBM thickening are common.
Gene pool = all alleles of all genes in a breeding population.
Family h/o of breast + ovarian Ca → BRCA1/2 (AD, DNA repair genes).\nP53 = Li-Fraumeni, PTEN = Cowden, CDH1 = hereditary diffuse gastric/lobular breast Ca.
BRCA testing uses sequencing (NGS/whole exome) to detect point mutations and small indels.
Mucosal neuroma belongs to MEN2B (RET), not TP53 (Li-Fraumeni: sarcoma, breast, brain, adrenocortical ca).
Pyroptosis = caspase-1/inflammasome-mediated lytic death c̅ IL-1β release (gasdermin D pores).
von Willebrand disease is the commonest inherited bleeding disorder (AD; defective platelet adhesion).
EPO helps anaemia of CKD (↓ renal EPO production); in aplastic/nutritional anaemia EPO is already high or cause is correctable.
Post-viral isolated thrombocytopenia c̅ normal smear = ITP → first-line oral corticosteroids.
G6PD→Haemolytic pattern: unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin ↑es, direct normal, urine urobilinogen ↑es.
Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii (lipophilic) → granulomatous lobular mastitis c̅ neutrophilic microabscesses.
Obesity-linked cancers include pancreas, meningioma and myeloma (also gastric cardia); non-cardia stomach cancer is not typically linked.
Granulosa cell tumour: Call-Exner bodies, coffee-bean nuclei, inhibin +ve; CA-125 is an epithelial ovarian tumour marker.
Congo red stains amyloid, not microorganisms; GMS and PAS stain fungi/Pneumocystis.
Only ~10-15% develop PUD, as ulcer needs host factors + virulence (CagA, VacA) + environmental factors (smoking, NSAIDs).\nMost infections stay asymptomatic.
SCID has no functional T cells → cannot mount graft rejection.
Terminal bronchiole: simple cuboidal ciliated epithelium c̅ Clara cells, no cartilage/glands/alveoli in wall.
Warburg effect: cancer cells prefer aerobic glycolysis (↑ glucose uptake and lactate) even when O₂ is available.
Dimeric secretory IgA (J chain + secretory component) predominates on mucosal surfaces.
Surface plasmon resonance measures real-time antigen-antibody binding kinetics (kon/koff) → affinity.
Procalcitonin-guided therapy allows early antibiotic discontinuation when levels fall.
